evidence: The AFM data demonstrate that after applying 100–150 cycles of HfCl4 and H2O on silicon substrates, the RMS surface roughness was comparable to the mean value of the film thickness (Table 1). Correspondingly, the relative surface roughness, which was determined as the ratio of the RMS roughness to the film thickness, was close to 1 and the growth of HfO2 was clearly three-dimensional in the HfCl4–H2O process under these conditions. All RHEED reflections of HfO2 shown in Fig. 5 can be attributed to a face-centered cubic phase with the lattice parameter of 0 :504 /C60:003 nm. With the increase of the film thickness to 10–15 nm, reflections of monoclinic phase also appeared. In the films, which were thicker than 30 nm, formation of only monoclinic phase was observed at the film surface.
